Theorem 1 — arbitrary mixed-side deletionACCEPTThe central identity is correct:

and therefore
$$\boxed{
v(X)=\frac{|X|+o(G-X)-o(G)}2.
}$$

Ordering each component, choosing the smaller bipartition side, and pairing consecutive vertices gives matching and cover certificates of equal size.There is no hidden assumption that removals must lie on one side of an initial cover. $$M_0\setminus L$$
survives as a matching in  $G-X$ . Consequently,
$$\nu(G)-\nu(G-X)\leq |L|.$$
Assigning distinct destroyed matching edges to the saving units is therefore valid.Importantly, the proof establishes global cardinality accounting, not local ownership of individual repair regions. $$O(2^{|K|}\operatorname{poly}(n)).$$
